keyChanges.title: Fremont production start window fully elapsed with no confirmation — Optimus still pre-production as of Aug 15
keyChanges.description: The late-July/August 2026 production start window that Elon Musk explicitly set on the Q1 2026 earnings call has now fully elapsed. As of August 15, 2026, Tesla has not issued any official statement, press release, X post, or production report confirming that a single Gen 3 Optimus unit has rolled off the Fremont first-generation line. The most recent authoritative data point remains the July 22, 2026 Q2 shareholder letter, which said Tesla is 'installing the first-generation lines for Optimus, where we expect to start production soon' and that output is 'anticipated later this year.' That language was already a retreat from the April Q1 guidance. The August window is now gone with no upgrade to that language. Tesla's July 2 production report contained zero Optimus count. No Optimus unit count, takt time, yield, or Academy delivery total has been published in the period August 6–15. The V3/Gen 3 full-body reveal — also promised for 'late July or August' — has also not occurred. In summary: two self-imposed milestones (production start and V3 reveal) have both been missed publicly, with Tesla defaulting to 'later this year' as the only remaining guidance.

positive_signals: Fremont facility conversion is physically complete — Model S/X lines decommissioned, new Optimus line infrastructure being installed
Musk visited the Fremont Optimus line on July 1 and posted a team photo, confirming transition is actively progressing
Tesla's app added Optimus-specific BLE authentication and home data consent UI strings (July 22 app update), showing software readiness work is underway
negative_signals: Late-July/August 2026 production start target — set explicitly by Musk on Q1 earnings — has now fully elapsed with no production confirmation from Tesla
V3/Gen 3 full-body reveal, also promised for 'late July or August,' has not occurred as of August 15
Most recent official language (July 22 Q2 letter) says lines are still 'being installed' and production 'anticipated later this year' — no upgrade in 24 days since Q2
Zero Optimus units appear in Tesla's production reports; the company has never disclosed a single production count
First builds are destined for the internal Optimus Academy for training data collection, not factory deployment or commercial use
Musk himself warned production will be 'extremely slow' and 'literally impossible to predict' — no guidance on even order-of-magnitude 2026 output
Chinese competitors (BYD Xiao Di, Unitree G1) are commercially deployed while Tesla is still in line-installation phase

key_metrics.actual: 0 confirmed Optimus units from Fremont Gen 1 line; production count never disclosed by Tesla
key_metrics.target: Late July–August 2026 start (Q1 guidance, elapsed); V3 reveal late July–August (Q1 guidance, elapsed); 'later this year' is current official guidance
key_metrics.trajectory: Production start effectively pushed to Q3–Q4 2026 at earliest; no evidence of acceleration

keyChanges.title: Giga Texas Optimus factory south perimeter beam emerges, locking building footprint — but production still 12+ months away
keyChanges.description: Drone footage captured by aerial observer Joe Tegtmeyer on August 7, 2026, and reported by Basenor, showed two concrete milestones at the dedicated Optimus factory being built at Giga Texas North Campus: (1) the north perimeter grade beam is fully formed with distinctive rounded corners, and (2) the south beam has now emerged, establishing the building's final length for the first time. Grade beams are the reinforced concrete perimeter foundations that lock a building's exact outer boundary — once poured, the footprint is fixed. The factory's total length is expected to exceed 4,000 feet, making it among the largest single manufacturing structures Tesla has ever built. The construction pace has been aggressive: official groundwork was confirmed in late May 2026, steel superstructure was clearing multiple floors by mid-June with seven cranes running simultaneously, and by July 20 the steel frame had stretched to 450 feet wide (expanding at roughly 8 feet per day). Context matters: this factory has a volume production target of Summer 2027 at the earliest. No robots will be produced here in 2026. The south beam milestone is a foundation-phase marker, not an operational milestone. The construction progress is on a trajectory consistent with a 2027 start, but it contributes zero to near-term production.

positive_signals: South perimeter grade beam emerged on August 7, establishing the final building footprint — a concrete foundation milestone
North perimeter grade beam fully formed with distinctive rounded corners by August 7
Construction pace remains aggressive: steel frame was growing at approximately 8 feet per day as of late July
7 cranes operating simultaneously confirm prioritized resource allocation
5.2M sq-ft footprint and 4,000+ foot length make this among Tesla's largest manufacturing structures
negative_signals: Volume production target is Summer 2027 — this factory produces zero Optimus robots in 2026
Grade beams are foundation-phase infrastructure; the factory is at a very early structural stage relative to commissioning
The 10M units/yr target has no precedent in complex manufacturing and remains aspirational
No manufacturing equipment, tooling, or production line components have been installed — years of interior buildout remain
Giga Texas Optimus factory construction progress does not change Fremont's inability to confirm production start

key_metrics.actual: South grade beam established Aug 7; north grade beam fully formed; steel frame at 450 ft wide as of July 20
key_metrics.target: Volume production Summer 2027; 10M units/yr eventual capacity
key_metrics.trajectory: Construction on track for 2027 target, but no 2026 production relevance

keyChanges.title: Musk shares Terafab concept render with Optimus — marketing vision, not a production update
keyChanges.description: On August 6, 2026, Elon Musk posted a Terafab concept render video on X. The video, credited to SpaceX, shows animated Optimus robots working the grounds of the planned Terafab facility at the Gibbons Creek site in Grimes County, Texas, alongside a Robovan traveling on an elevated roadway and a Tesla Semi and Cybercab in frame. Musk wrote: 'Terafab Texas will be the largest and most valuable building on Earth by far.' The video was covered by Teslarati. Critical context: this is a CGI concept render, not footage of actual Optimus robots operating. The Terafab facility is still in design and permitting phases. Optimus itself cannot currently confirm production has started at Fremont. The render depicts a long-term aspirational future state, not a current operational reality. The Robovan in the same video has no confirmed production timeline. Neither does the render reveal any new Optimus hardware, capability, or production specification. This is brand-building content released during the period when Tesla should have been announcing Fremont production start — instead it is providing marketing imagery of a facility that does not yet exist featuring a robot whose production has not yet been confirmed.

positive_signals: Terafab render confirms Optimus is central to Tesla's long-term manufacturing vision
Musk's continued public promotion of Optimus signals the program remains a strategic priority
negative_signals: The video is CGI concept art, not footage of operating Optimus robots — zero production information conveyed
Published on August 6, the first day of the window when Tesla should have been confirming Fremont production start — instead delivered a concept render
Terafab facility itself is in early-stage planning and does not exist operationally
Robovan also shown in the render has no confirmed production timeline — both products in the video are pre-production
The render distracts from the absence of any Fremont production confirmation during the elapsed Q1-guided window

categoryUpdate.latestStatus: Fremont first-gen Optimus production lines still being installed as of late July 2026; no official production confirmation through August 15 despite late-July/August target having fully elapsed. Giga Texas dedicated Optimus factory south perimeter grade beam established Aug 7, locking building footprint — but volume production target remains Summer 2027. V3/Gen 3 full-body reveal also promised for late July/August has not occurred.
